labels.expectedFinding: aún meaning todavía is tonic and written with the accent; aun without accent means incluso/hasta.
Existential haber stays singular in every tense: «hubo dos accidentes», not «hubieron».
In the 12-hour model the part of the day is given by de la mañana/tarde/noche; without it «a las diez» can be 10:00 or 22:00, and a meeting at either is plausible.
se before lo/la/los/las is an invariable variant of both le and les, so it does not show whether the recipient is one person or several.
The imperfecto presents a past situation in its course, the indefinido as a finished whole; the sentence gives no duration or other cue that excludes the finished-episode reading.
At A1-03-L3 only the present of estar is taught; the task can only be answered with the imperfecto «estaba» and the past frame «llegamos», both introduced in A2.
ahí is the adverb of place (Déjalo ahí, sobre la mesa); hay is a form of haber; ay is an interjection.
Buenos días is the morning greeting of general Spanish (buen día predominates in American Spanish).
Option feedback must agree with the option's outcome; an incorrect option that tells the learner «Правильно!» is conflicting feedback.
A delayed task is a held-out prompt for later review; displaying the identical sentence as an example turns recall into copying.
deber + infinitive without de is preferably used for obligation; deber de + infinitive preferably for supposition.
delante de mí is the recommended pattern in the common language, and the pronoun mí carries the diacritic accent.
